Transboundary Water Cooperation Report 2025

By Leila Haddad and Tomás Ruiz January 22, 2025

Shared rivers supply water to more than 40 percent of the world’s population, yet fewer than half of the 26 basins we track have a functioning joint management body. This year’s report reviews the agreements, data-sharing arrangements and disputes recorded across those basins during 2024.

Key findings

  • Eleven of the 26 basins exchanged hydrological data at least monthly in 2024, up from seven in 2020.
  • Formal disputes were lodged in four basins, all of them during the dry season.
  • Basins with a joint commission reported 35 percent fewer supply interruptions downstream.

Basin-by-basin results

The table summarizes the cooperation score (0–10) we assign to each basin, based on treaty coverage, data exchange and dispute resolution.

Recommendations

Basin authorities should publish monitoring data in open formats within 30 days of collection and establish standing dispute-resolution panels before, not during, the dry season.
